::: {#exm-flat-prior-reparam}
#### A flat prior on a probability is not flat on its log-odds

A [flat prior](#def-flat-prior) is flat only on the scale on which it is stated.
Let $\pi$ have the uniform prior of @exm-prior,
and let $\eta \eqdef \logit(\pi)$ be its log-odds,
so that $\pi = \expit(\eta) = 1 / (1 + e^{-\eta})$.
The derivative of $\expit$ is

$$
\ba
\frac{d}{d\eta} \expit(\eta)
&= \frac{d}{d\eta} (1 + e^{-\eta})^{-1}\\
&= -(1 + e^{-\eta})^{-2} \cdot (-e^{-\eta})
&& \text{(chain rule)}\\
&= \frac{1}{1 + e^{-\eta}} \cdot \frac{e^{-\eta}}{1 + e^{-\eta}}
&& \text{(splitting the fraction)}\\
&= \expit(\eta)\, \paren{1 - \expit(\eta)}
&& \text{($\tfrac{e^{-\eta}}{1 + e^{-\eta}} = 1 - \tfrac{1}{1 + e^{-\eta}}$)}.
\ea
$$

By the change-of-variables formula for densities
[@CaseBerg01, Theorem 2.1.5],
the prior density of $\eta$ is

$$
\ba
\p_\eta(\eta)
&= \p_\pi\paren{\expit(\eta)} \cdot \abs{\frac{d}{d\eta} \expit(\eta)}
&& \text{(change of variables)}\\
&= 1 \cdot \expit(\eta)\, \paren{1 - \expit(\eta)}
&& \text{(uniform density of $\pi$; derivative of $\expit$)},
\ea
$$

the standard logistic density,
which peaks at $\eta = 0$ and decays in both directions.
Under this prior,
$\Pr(-1 < \eta < 1) = \expit(1) - \expit(-1) \approx `r round(stats::plogis(1) - stats::plogis(-1), 2)`$,
whereas a flat prior on $\eta$ would make every interval of length 2 equally likely.
"Noninformative" therefore depends on the parameterization.
:::
